results.title: L1 norm of a polynomial
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $K$ be a semiring and $v$ a real-valued absolute value on $K$. The L1 norm of a polynomial $p = \sum_i a_i X^i \in K[X]$ with respect to $v$ is the real number $\|p\|_v = \sum_i v(a_i)$, where the sum runs over the indices $i$ with $a_i \neq 0$.

results.title: L1 norm as a sum over the support
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a semiring and $v$ a real-valued absolute value on $K$. For every polynomial $p = \sum_i a_i X^i \in K[X]$, the L1 norm $\|p\|_v$ of $p$ with respect to $v$ equals $\sum_{i \in S} v(a_i)$, where $S = \{ i : a_i \neq 0 \}$ is the support of $p$.

results.title: L1 norm of the zero polynomial
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a semiring and $v$ a real-valued absolute value on $K$. The L1 norm of the zero polynomial in $K[X]$ with respect to $v$ is $0$.

results.title: Nonnegativity of the L1 norm
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a semiring and $v$ a real-valued absolute value on $K$. For every polynomial $p \in K[X]$, the L1 norm of $p$ with respect to $v$ satisfies $\|p\|_v \ge 0$.

results.title: L1 norm as a sum up to the degree
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a semiring and $v$ a real-valued absolute value on $K$. Let $p = \sum_i a_i X^i \in K[X]$ and let $n$ be the degree of $p$, with $n = 0$ when $p = 0$. Then the L1 norm of $p$ with respect to $v$ is $\|p\|_v = \sum_{i=0}^{n} v(a_i)$.

results.title: L1 norm of a monic polynomial
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a nontrivial semiring (one with $0 \neq 1$) and $v$ a real-valued absolute value on $K$. If $f = \sum_i a_i X^i \in K[X]$ is monic of degree $n$, then the L1 norm of $f$ with respect to $v$ is $\|f\|_v = \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} v(a_i) + 1$.

results.title: Monic polynomials have L1 norm at least one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a nontrivial semiring (one with $0 \neq 1$) and $v$ a real-valued absolute value on $K$. If $f \in K[X]$ is monic, then the L1 norm of $f$ with respect to $v$ satisfies $\|f\|_v \ge 1$.

results.title: Monic polynomials close in L1 norm have the same degree
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ be a nontrivial ring and $v$ a real-valued absolute value on $K$. If $f, g \in K[x]$ are monic and the L1 norm of $f - g$ with respect to $v$ is strictly less than $1$, then $f$ and $g$ have the same degree.

results.title: Root bound by the L1 norm
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $K$ and $L$ be fields with $L$ a $K$-algebra, let $v$ be a real-valued absolute value on $K$, and let $w$ be a real-valued absolute value on $L$ lying over $v$, that is, $w(x) = v(x)$ for every $x \in K$ viewed in $L$ through the algebra map. If $f$ is a monic polynomial over $K$ and $\alpha \in L$ is a root of $f$, then $w(\alpha)$ is strictly less than the L1 norm of $f$ with respect to $v$.

results.title: Tribonacci numbers that are products of factorials
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $(T_n)_{n \in \mathbb{Z}}$ be the integer sequence with $T_0 = 0$, $T_1 = T_2 = 1$ and $T_{j+3} = T_{j+2} + T_{j+1} + T_j$ for every integer $j$. If $n$ is an integer such that $|T_n| = m_1! \, m_2! \cdots m_k!$ for some $k \ge 1$ and some positive integers $m_1, \dots, m_k$, then $n \in \{-9, -8, -7, -5, -3, -2, 1, 2, 3, 4, 7\}$.

results.title: Morse quadratic form
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $k$ and $n$, the Morse quadratic form of index $k$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$, with coordinates $v_0, \dots, v_{n-1}$, is the function $Q_{k,n} \colon \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ given by $Q_{k,n}(v) = \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} \varepsilon_i v_i^2$, where $\varepsilon_i = -1$ if $i < k$ and $\varepsilon_i = 1$ if $i \ge k$. In particular, if $k \ge n$ every coefficient is $-1$.

results.title: The Morse quadratic form vanishes at the origin
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: For all natural numbers $k$ and $n$, the Morse quadratic form $Q_{k,n}$ of index $k$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ satisfies $Q_{k,n}(0) = 0$.

results.title: Smoothness of the Morse quadratic form
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: For all natural numbers $k$ and $n$, the Morse quadratic form $Q_{k,n} \colon \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ of index $k$ is $C^\infty$.

results.title: The Morse quadratic form of index zero
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: For every natural number $n$, the Morse quadratic form $Q_{0,n}$ of index $0$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ satisfies $Q_{0,n}(v) = \|v\|^2$ for every $v \in \mathbb{R}^n$, where $\|v\|$ is the Euclidean norm of $v$.

results.title: The Morse quadratic form when the index is at least the dimension
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: If $n \le k$, then the Morse quadratic form $Q_{k,n}$ of index $k$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ satisfies $Q_{k,n}(v) = -\|v\|^2$ for every $v \in \mathbb{R}^n$, where $\|v\|$ is the Euclidean norm of $v$.

results.title: Multiplicity of a root of $f = w$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and $w, z \in \mathbb{C}$. The multiplicity of $z$ as a root of the equation $f = w$ is an extended natural number: it is $\infty$ if $f(t) = w$ for every $t \neq z$ in some neighbourhood of $z$; otherwise it is $n$ if $f - w$ has meromorphic order $n \ge 0$ at $z$, and it is $0$ if that order is negative or $f - w$ is not meromorphic at $z$.

results.title: Multiplicity of a pole
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and $z \in \mathbb{C}$. The multiplicity of $z$ as a pole of $f$, that is, the multiplicity of the value $\infty$ at $z$, is $-n$ if $f$ has finite meromorphic order $n < 0$ at $z$, and $0$ otherwise. In particular it is $0$ unless $f$ has a pole at $z$.

results.title: Multiplicity of a value on the Riemann sphere
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and $z \in \mathbb{C}$, and let $w$ be a point of the Riemann sphere $\mathbb{C} \cup \{\infty\}$. The multiplicity of $w$ as a value of $f$ at $z$ is the multiplicity of $z$ as a root of $f = w$ when $w$ is finite, and the multiplicity of $z$ as a pole of $f$ when $w = \infty$.

results.title: Bounded value distribution
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ has bounded value distribution if for every real $r > 0$ there is a natural number $C$ such that, for every value $w$ of the Riemann sphere $\mathbb{C} \cup \{\infty\}$ and every open disc of radius $r$, the multiplicities of $w$ as a value of $f$ at the points of any finite subset of the disc add up to at most $C$.

results.title: Discrete Fourier transform on a finite abelian group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group and $f : G \to \mathbb{C}$. The discrete Fourier transform of $f$ is the function on the additive characters $\psi$ of $G$ with values in $\mathbb{C}$ (maps with $\psi(0) = 1$ and $\psi(a + b) = \psi(a)\psi(b)$) given by $\hat f(\psi) = \sum_{x \in G} \psi(x) f(x)$.

Then for every $x \in G$, $f(x) = \frac{1}{|G|} \sum_{\psi} \overline{\psi(x)} \, \hat f(\psi)$, where $\psi$ runs over all additive characters of $G$ with values in…

Then $\sum_{x \in G} \overline{f(x)} \, g(x)$ equals $\frac{1}{|G|} \sum_{\psi} \overline{\hat f(\psi)} \, \hat g(\psi)$, where $\psi$ runs over all…

results.title: Translation modulates the discrete Fourier transform
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, $f : G \to \mathbb{C}$, $t \in G$, and $\psi$ an additive character of $G$ with values in $\mathbb{C}$, and write $\hat h(\psi) = \sum_{x \in G} \psi(x) h(x)$ for the discrete Fourier transform of $h : G \to \mathbb{C}$. If $g(x) = f(x - t)$ for all $x \in G$, then $\hat g(\psi) = \psi(t) \hat f(\psi)$.

results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all real numbers $a$, $b$, $\delta$ and $x$, the interval cutoff $\chi_{a,b,\delta}$ with endpoints $a$, $b$ and width $\delta$ satisfies $0 \le \chi_{a,b,\delta}(x)$.

results.title: The interval cutoff is at most one

results.title: Continuity of the interval cutoff
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all real numbers $a$, $b$ and $\delta$, including $\delta = 0$, the interval cutoff $\chi_{a,b,\delta} \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ with endpoints $a$, $b$ and width $\delta$ is continuous.

results.title: Convergence of a series in order
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a sequence $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ and $a \in \mathbb{R}$, the series $\sum_n f(n)$ converges in order to $a$ when its partial sums $\sum_{n=0}^{N-1} f(n)$ tend to $a$ as $N \to \infty$.

results.title: Convergence in order via partial sums
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a sequence $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ and $a \in \mathbb{R}$, the series $\sum_n f(n)$ converges in order to $a$ if and only if its partial sums $\sum_{n=0}^{N-1} f(n)$ tend to $a$ as $N \to \infty$.

results.title: Terms of a convergent series tend to zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ and the series $\sum_n f(n)$ converges in order to some $s \in \mathbb{R}$, then $f(n) \to 0$ as $n \to \infty$.

results.title: Riemann rearrangement theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ be such that the series $\sum_n f(n)$ converges in order to some real number, while the series $\sum_n |f(n)|$ is not summable. Then for every $a \in \mathbb{R}$ there is a permutation $\sigma$ of $\mathbb{N}$ such that the rearranged series $\sum_n f(\sigma(n))$ converges in order to $a$.

results.title: The central binomial series in $\sin x$ and $x \log|2\sin x|$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $x$ be a real number with $|x| \le \pi/2$, and let $L(x) = x \log|2\sin x|$ for $x \ne 0$ and $L(0) = 0$. Then $|2\sin x| > 0$ if $x \ne 0$, the series $S(x) = \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \binom{2k}{k} \frac{\sin^{2k+1} x}{2^{2k} (2k+1)^2}$ and $F(x) = \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{\sin 2kx}{k^2}$ are both summable, and $S(x) = L(x) + \frac{1}{2} F(x)$.

results.title: The central binomial series in $\cos x$ minus that in $\sin x$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $x$ be a real number with $0 \le x \le \pi/4$, and for real $y$ let $S(y) = \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \binom{2k}{k} \frac{\sin^{2k+1} y}{2^{2k} (2k+1)^2}$. Then $2\cos x > 0$, the series $D(x) = \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \binom{2k}{k} \frac{\cos^{2k+1} x - \sin^{2k+1} x} {2^{2k} (2k+1)^2}$ and the series defining $S(2x)$ are both summable, and $D(x) = \frac{\pi}{2} \log(2\cos x) - \frac{1}{2} S(2x)$.

results.title: The central binomial series in $\cos x$ plus that in $\sin x$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $x$ be a real number with $0 \le x \le \pi/4$. Then $2\cos x > 0$, the series $C(x) = \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \binom{2k}{k} \frac{\cos^{2k+1} x + \sin^{2k+1} x} {2^{2k} (2k+1)^2}$ and $T(x) = \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} (-1)^k \frac{\tan^{2k+1} x}{(2k+1)^2}$ are both summable, and $C(x) = \frac{\pi}{2} \log(2\cos x) + T(x)$.

results.title: Ramanujan's central-binomial sine series identity (Entry 31)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For real $y$ let $\psi(y) = \sum_{k \ge 0} \binom{2k}{k} \sin^{2k+1}(\pi y) / \bigl(2^{2k} (2k+1)^2\bigr)$. If $0 \le x \le 1/4$, then the series defining $\psi(1/2 - x)$, $\psi(2x)$ and $\psi(x)$ converge absolutely, $2 \cos(\pi x) > 0$, and $\psi(1/2 - x) + \tfrac12 \psi(2x) - \psi(x) = \tfrac{\pi}{2} \log(2 \cos(\pi x))$.

results.title: Mapping theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The image `η ∘ T⁻¹` of a Poisson point process under a measurable map `T : E → F` is the Poisson point process with intensity `μ ∘ T⁻¹` (Last–Penrose Thm. 5.1).

results.title: Restriction theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The restrictions `η|_{A i}` of a Poisson point process with finite intensity `μ` to pairwise disjoint measurable sets `A i` are independent Poisson point processes with intensities `μ|_{A i}` (Last–Penrose Thm. 5.2).

results.title: Ordered representation count
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a set $A$ of natural numbers and a natural number $n$, the ordered representation count of $n$ by $A$ is the number of ordered pairs $(a, b) \in A \times A$ with $a + b = n$. Pairs are not identified under swapping: when $a \ne b$, the pairs $(a, b)$ and $(b, a)$ are counted separately.

results.title: Positivity of the ordered representation count
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a set $A$ of natural numbers and a natural number $n$, the number of ordered pairs $(a, b) \in A \times A$ with $a + b = n$ is positive if and only if $n = a + b$ for some $a \in A$ and $b \in A$.

results.title: Statement of Erdős Problem 1112 for gaps in $(2, 3)$ and triple sums
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The threshold $r_3(2, 3)$ exists: there is a natural number $r$ such that for every strictly increasing sequence $b_0 < b_1 < \cdots$ of positive integers with $b_{i+1} \ge r b_i$ for all $i$, there is a sequence $a_0, a_1, \dots$ of positive integers with $a_i + 2 \le a_{i+1} \le a_i + 3$ for all $i$ such that no $b_i$ is a sum $x + y + z$ of three, not necessarily distinct, terms $x, y, z$ of the sequence $a$.

results.title: Orientations of a graph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a vertex set $V$. A binary relation $D$ on $V$ is an orientation of $G$ if $D(u, v)$ holds only when $u$ and $v$ are adjacent in $G$, and for every pair of adjacent vertices $u$ and $v$ exactly one of $D(u, v)$ and $D(v, u)$ holds.

results.title: Closed directed walks
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $D$ be a binary relation on a set $V$, viewed as a digraph, let $n$ be a natural number, and let $f_0, f_1, \dots, f_{n+1}$ be elements of $V$. The sequence $(f_0, \dots, f_{n+1})$ is a closed directed walk of length $n + 1$ in $D$ if $f_0 = f_{n+1}$ and $D(f_i, f_{i+1})$ holds for every $i$ with $0 \le i \le n$.

results.title: Dichromatically $k$-colourable graphs
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a vertex set $V$ and let $k$ be a natural number. Then $G$ is dichromatically $k$-colourable if for every orientation $D$ of $G$ there is a map $c \colon V \to \{0, \dots, k - 1\}$, not required to be a proper colouring, such that no closed directed walk of positive length in $D$ has all of its vertices of the same colour under $c$.

results.title: Dichromatic number
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The dichromatic number of a simple graph $G$ is the least natural number $k$ such that $G$ is dichromatically $k$-colourable, taken in $\mathbb{N} \cup \{\infty\}$; it is $\infty$ if $G$ is dichromatically $k$-colourable for no natural number $k$.

results.title: The dichromatic number as a least natural number
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph. If $G$ is dichromatically $n$-colourable for some natural number $n$, then the dichromatic number of $G$ equals the least natural number $k$ such that $G$ is dichromatically $k$-colourable.

results.title: The empty orientation of an edgeless graph
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a simple graph $G$ has no edges, then the empty relation on its vertex set, the digraph with no arcs, is an orientation of $G$.

results.title: Edgeless graphs are dichromatically $1$-colourable
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a simple graph $G$ has no edges, then $G$ is dichromatically $1$-colourable.

results.title: Pushdown automaton
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A pushdown automaton over an input alphabet $T$, with states in $\sigma$ and stack alphabet $\Gamma$, consists of a transition function, a start state in $\sigma$ and an initial stack symbol in $\Gamma$. The transition function assigns to each state $q$, each input option (a letter of $T$, or none for an $\varepsilon$-transition) and each popped stack symbol $\gamma$ a finite set of pairs $(q', u)$ of a next state…

results.title: Pushdown automaton configuration
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A configuration of a pushdown automaton with input alphabet $T$, states in $\sigma$ and stack alphabet $\Gamma$ consists of a current state in $\sigma$, the remaining unread input (a word over $T$), and the stack contents (a list over $\Gamma$ whose first element is the top of the stack).

results.title: Multi-step computation of a pushdown automaton
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For a pushdown automaton $M$, a configuration $c$ derives a configuration $c'$ when $M$ can reach $c'$ from $c$ in zero or more computation steps; that is, derivation is the reflexive transitive closure of the one-step computation relation of $M$.

results.title: Finitely supported pushdown automata
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A pushdown automaton $M$ is finitely supported when there are finite sets $\sigma_0$ of states, $\Gamma_0$ of stack symbols and $T_0$ of input letters such that the start state lies in $\sigma_0$, the initial stack symbol lies in $\Gamma_0$, every transition from a state in $\sigma_0$ that pops a symbol in $\Gamma_0$ (on any input letter or on $\varepsilon$) moves to a state in $\sigma_0$ and pushes only symbols in…

results.title: Initial configuration of a pushdown automaton
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The initial configuration of a pushdown automaton $M$ on an input word $w$ has the start state of $M$ as its state, all of $w$ as its remaining input, and the stack consisting of the initial stack symbol of $M$ alone.

results.title: Language accepted by a pushdown automaton
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The language accepted by a pushdown automaton $M$, by empty stack, consists of the words $w$ for which some computation of $M$ leads from the initial configuration on input $w$ to a configuration, in some state, with no remaining input and an empty stack.

results.title: Closed sets of stack symbols
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A finite set $\Gamma_0$ of stack symbols is closed for a pushdown automaton $M$ when every transition of $M$ that pops a symbol in $\Gamma_0$, from any state and on any input letter or on $\varepsilon$, pushes only symbols in $\Gamma_0$. Computations starting with a stack inside a closed set keep their stack inside it.

results.title: Lifting a stack to a set of stack symbols
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a finite set $\Gamma_0$ of stack symbols and a stack $s = \gamma_1 \cdots \gamma_n$ all of whose symbols lie in $\Gamma_0$, the lifted stack is the same list $\gamma_1 \cdots \gamma_n$, in the same order, regarded as a stack over the alphabet $\Gamma_0$.

results.summary: Let $M$ be a pushdown automaton and let $\Gamma_0$ be a finite set of stack symbols that contains the initial stack symbol of $M$ and is closed for $M$. results.title: Computations stay inside a closed set of stack symbols
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be a pushdown automaton and $\Gamma_0$ a finite set of stack symbols that is closed for $M$. If a configuration $c$ derives a configuration $c'$ in zero or more steps of $M$, and every symbol on the stack of $c$ lies in $\Gamma_0$, then every symbol on the stack of $c'$ lies in $\Gamma_0$.

Then the symbols of $s'$ also lie in $\Gamma_0$, and…

results.title: Restricting the stack alphabet preserves the accepted language
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $M$ be a pushdown automaton and let $\Gamma_0$ be a finite set of stack symbols of $M$ that contains the initial stack symbol of $M$ and is closed for $M$. Then the restriction of $M$ to the stack alphabet $\Gamma_0$ accepts, by empty stack, exactly the same language as $M$.
